tagline: Finance student at the intersection of markets, AI, and law
about.p1: I'm Cheng-Mou (Momo) Chen 陳政謀, a sophomore at the McCombs School of Business at UT Austin, planning to declare Finance alongside a BA in Economics. I build things where capital markets, technology, and the rules that govern them overlap.
about.p2: My work runs in three directions: quantitative projects like a factor-investing backtest engine, AI tools built for a research team at the UT School of Nursing, and legal writing on securities regulation and AI copyright. I'm headed toward management consulting, and possibly corporate law in finance and securities regulation.
about.p3: I'm fluent in English and Mandarin, read and write both Traditional and Simplified Chinese, and split my time between Austin and Taiwan. Take a look at my work, download my resume, or reach me at cc79336@eid.utexas.edu or on LinkedIn.
w1.lead: More than 10 years of S&P 500 data, tested factor by factor. I built quintile long-short portfolios on momentum, value, size, and quality, plus a multi-factor composite.
w1.b1: Reports Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and factor correlations for each strategy.
w1.b2: An 8-stage ETL pipeline makes sure every signal uses only data available at the time, so results carry no look-ahead bias.
w2.lead: A 12-term path to law school, made into a game. A full-stack web app that breaks law school prep into concrete milestones, term by term.
w2.b1: Custom MongoDB schema and its own authentication.
w2.b2: A public read-only view to share with advisors, and a private edit mode for the student.
w3.t: AI Outreach Agents, UT School of Nursing
w3.lead: Outreach volume up 75%; response rate up 25%. I built two AI agents, on Claude and Microsoft Copilot, that find relevant Asian American and cancer-support organizations for Dr. Wonshik Chee's research team.
w3.b1: The agents turned a manual search into a repeatable pipeline for community recruitment.
w3.b2: Bilingual English/Chinese email templates drove the higher response rate.
w3.tools: Claude, Microsoft Copilot, prompt design, bilingual outreach
w4.t: Aligna Landing Page Audit, Texas Marketrics
w4.lead: Click-through up 30%, and the startup's first 10 paying users. I audited Aligna's landing page and recommended changes, then ran a product-channel fit analysis to find which acquisition channels to test first.
w4.tools: Funnel analysis, product-channel fit, conversion copy
e1.d: Growth and go-to-market work for early-stage clients, including the Aligna engagement.
e2.d: Authored two published legal interpellations, on higher education and on AI copyright.
e3.d: Community-based recruitment and data analysis for Chinese and Chinese American study populations.
e4.d: Writes and edits pieces on securities regulation and AI copyright law.
wr1.d: How the human-authorship requirement applies when generative AI produces the work.
wr2.d: Formal questions to the executive on higher education policy.
wr3.d: Questions on how Taiwan's copyright framework should treat AI training and AI-generated content.
sk.fin.v: Factor investing, backtesting, Bloomberg Market Concepts
